why_use_this: Reach for this package when you need to manipulate a mathematical expression AS an expression -- differentiate it symbolically, simplify it, substitute values and evaluate it, print it back out -- rather than just computing a single numeric answer. This is what distinguishes it from every other numeric package in the ecosystem: [vani-calculus](https://github.com/enthusiasticgeek/vani-calculus)'s `diff_central` gives you a NUMBER (the derivative's value at one point); `sym_diff` gives you a new EXPRESSION (the derivative as a formula you can still evaluate anywhere, print, or differentiate again). Expressions live in a flat `Vec<ExprNode>` arena addressed by `i64` index rather than as a recursive struct/enum -- a deliberate workaround for v1's lack of self-referential types, not a stylistic choice (see the README's "Encoding" section for why a naive recursive `enum Expr` doesn't compile). Despite what the README's "What this library does NOT provide (yet)" section currently claims ("Integration, equation solving" as unimplemented "later phases"), this package (per its function list) actually already includes `sym_integrate`, `sym_solve_equation_le2`, `poly_factor_rational`, and `sym_factor_rational` -- reach for those directly rather than assuming you need to wait for a future version.

math_notes.sym_add: Builds a new `Add(a, b)` node representing \( a + b \) -- pure tree construction, no evaluation or simplification happens at build time (that's `sym_eval`/`sym_simplify`'s job).
math_notes.sym_sub: Builds a new `Sub(a, b)` node representing \( a - b \).
math_notes.sym_mul: Builds a new `Mul(a, b)` node representing \( a \times b \).
math_notes.sym_div: Builds a new `Div(a, b)` node representing \( a / b \).
math_notes.sym_pow: Builds a new `Pow(base, exponent)` node representing \( \text{base}^{\text{exponent}} \) -- `sym_eval` only accepts a nonnegative-integer exponent value at evaluation time; the node itself can be built with any exponent subexpression.
math_notes.sym_eval: Recursively evaluates the expression tree rooted at `root` to a single `i64`, substituting each `Var` node's value from `var_values[var_id]` -- strict evaluation (both operands of a binary op are always evaluated, even ones an outer simplification could have skipped), and traps if a `Pow` node's exponent is negative (only nonnegative integer powers are supported).
math_notes.sym_simplify: Builds a simplified COPY of the tree into a separate arena `dst` (never mutates `src` in place): folds `Num op Num` into a single `Num`, applies algebraic identities (\( x \cdot 1 \to x \), \( x \cdot 0 \to 0 \), \( x/1 \to x \), \( x^1 \to x \), \( x^0 \to 1 \), \( -(-x) \to x \)), and collects like terms across a flattened `Add`/`Sub` chain (\( 2x+3x \to 5x \), \( x-x \to 0 \)) -- deliberately not full polynomial normal form; see the README's "Simplification scope" for the exact boundary (e.g. \( 2(3x) \) does NOT fold to \( 6x \), since that needs multiplicative-factor combination this pass doesn't do).
math_notes.sym_diff: Symbolic differentiation with respect to `var_id`, one rule per node kind, appending new nodes to the SAME arena `root` lives in (reusing existing node indices for any unchanged subexpression, e.g. `v` in the product rule): \( \dfrac{d}{dx}c=0 \), \( \dfrac{d}{dx}x=1 \) (else 0), \( (u+v)'=u'+v' \), \( (u-v)'=u'-v' \), \( (-u)'=-u' \), \( (uv)'=u'v+uv' \) (product rule), \( (u/v)' = \dfrac{u'v-uv'}{v^2} \) (quotient rule), \( (u^n)' = n\,u^{n-1}u' \) (power + chain rule, \( n \) must be a literal). Output is deliberately NOT simplified -- pipe the result through `sym_simplify` to fold away terms like `1*x` or `x^1` the raw rules produce.
math_notes.sym_poly_coeffs_le2: Extracts polynomial coefficients (up to degree 2: \( c_0 + c_1x + c_2x^2 \)) from an expression tree with respect to `var_id`, by flattening the same `Add`/`Sub` chain `sym_simplify` collects like-terms across -- the bridge between the tree representation and a plain coefficient `Vec` that a numeric solver like [vani-algebra](https://github.com/enthusiasticgeek/vani-algebra) can consume.
math_notes.sym_solve_poly_le2: Solves `p(x) = 0` for a degree-\( \le 2 \) polynomial extracted via `sym_poly_coeffs_le2`, by handing the coefficients off to [vani-algebra](https://github.com/enthusiasticgeek/vani-algebra)'s numeric root-finder (the compiler's own `f64_quadratic_root` for the quadratic case) -- symbolic extraction feeding a numeric solve, not a symbolic solution.
math_notes.sym_solve_equation_le2: Solves `lhs = rhs` (two separate expression trees) for `var_id` by first rewriting it as `lhs - rhs = 0` (a single expression) and then applying the same degree-\( \le 2 \) polynomial solve as `sym_solve_poly_le2`.
